summary: The article argues that social media's effect on adolescent mental health is complex rather than simply harmful. It debunks the 'more screen time equals more harm' myth, noting that quality of use matters, and that social media often amplifies existing issues rather than causing them. It also highlights positive uses such as community-finding, and describes literacy initiatives, campaigns, and policy and family efforts to promote healthier use.
one_line: Article explaining that social media's impact on teen mental health is nuanced, covering myths, benefits, risks, and education, community, and policy responses.
key_facts: The article is dated as of September 15, 2023 and discusses social media's impact on adolescent mental health.

Dr. Lisa Moreno, a clinical psychologist specializing in adolescent health, argues that social media offers a sense of belonging but presents a curated version of reality that can provoke inadequacy and loneliness.
The Summit Counseling Center's director reports a sharp rise in cases of self-doubt and social anxiety since January 2024.
The Digital Wellness Institute and similar groups found that quality, not just quantity, of social media interaction plays a crucial role in mental health impact.
Tech analyst and writer Jeremy Olson said in a webinar on February 9, 2024 that how teens use social media (creative expression, genuine connection, or passive scrolling) vastly alters its effects.

Melanie Sanders, a school counselor whose work was the subject of a PBS special aired on October 20, 2023, says social media amplifies body image concerns, bullying, and depression by exposing teens to triggers 24/7.
The 'Fitter, Happier, More Productive' campaign was launched on December 1, 2023 by a coalition of mental health organizations to foster a supportive, authentic online environment.
Educator and author Sandra Mitchell established the Social Savvy Project on September 5, 2023 to improve young people's digital literacy.
Dr. Alex Hart published a study on teen social media use in Youth & Society on November 12, 2023, highlighting that social media helps marginalized teens find community.
Media consultant Dr. Grace Kim recommended personalized, tailored approaches in her keynote at the Social Media and Mental Health Symposium on September 25, 2023.
Parenting blogger Emily Torres introduced 'Family Digital Detox Week' on January 14, 2024 to encourage breaks from social media.
Media literacy campaigns in schools are gaining traction, and content regulation is being discussed in political arenas.
